actions: compare offered certificate with existing keyring certificate

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If the user authorizes this certificate, it SHOULD be added to the keyring alongside any previous value(s) for this address-of-record.
actions: add certificate to keyring alongside previous values for this address-of-record

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If a UA receives an S/MIME body that has been encrypted with a public key unknown to the recipient, it MUST reject the request with a 493 (Undecipherable) response.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Note that a user agent that receives a request containing an S/MIME body that is not optional (with a Content-Disposition header "handling" parameter of "required") MUST reject the request with a 415 Unsupported Media Type response if the MIME type is not understood.
actions: reject request with 415 Unsupported Media Type response

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: A user agent that receives such a response when S/MIME is sent SHOULD notify its user that the remote device does not support S/MIME, and it MAY subsequently resend the request without S/MIME, if appropriate; however, this 415 response may constitute a downgrade attack.
actions: notify user that remote device does not support S/MIME

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a user agent sends an S/MIME body in a request, but receives a response that contains a MIME body that is not secured, the UAC SHOULD notify its user that the session could not be secured.
actions: notify user that session could not be secured

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: However, if a user agent that supports S/MIME receives a request with an unsecured body, it SHOULD NOT respond with a secured body, but if it expects S/MIME from the sender (for example, because the sender's From header field value corresponds to an identity on its keychain), the UAS SHOULD notify its user that the session could not be secured.
actions: do not respond with secured body

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Finally, if during the course of a dialog a UA receives a certificate in a CMS SignedData message that does not correspond with the certificates previously exchanged during a dialog, the UA MUST notify its user of the change, preferably in terms that indicate that this is a potential security breach.
actions: notify user of certificate change indicating potential security breach

statements.subject: client
statements.description: UACs MAY send an initial request such as an OPTIONS message with a CMS detached signature in order to solicit the certificate of the remote side (the signature SHOULD be over a "message/sip" body of the type described in Section 23.4).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a UAS receives a request that contains a tunneled "message/sip" S/MIME body, it SHOULD include a tunneled "message/sip" body in the response with the same smime-type.
actions: Include tunneled "message/sip" body in the response
Set smime-type of tunneled body to match that of the received request

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the From header field in an encrypted body differs from the value in the "outer" message, the value within the encrypted body SHOULD be displayed to the user, but MUST NOT be used in the "outer" header fields of any future messages.
actions: display encrypted body From value to user

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: They SHOULD NOT however be used in the "outer" headers of any future messages.
actions: do not use encrypted end-to-end header fields in outer headers of any future messages

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If present, the Date header field MUST always be the same in the "inner" and "outer" headers.
actions: ensure Date header field value is identical in inner and outer headers

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: UAs SHOULD never include these in an "inner" message if they are not included in the "outer" message.
actions: do not include low-utility header fields in inner message when absent from outer message

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: UAs that receive any of these header fields in an encrypted body SHOULD ignore the encrypted values.
actions: ignore encrypted values of low-utility header fields received in encrypted body

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If a SIP UA encounters an unknown header field with an integrity violation, it MUST ignore the header field.
actions: ignore the unknown header field with integrity violation

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If a Date header is present in a message with a signed body, the recipient SHOULD compare the header field value with its own internal clock, if applicable.
actions: compare Date header field value with internal clock

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If a significant time discrepancy is detected (on the order of an hour or more), the user agent SHOULD alert the user to the anomaly, and note that it is a potential security breach.
actions: note that the anomaly is a potential security breach

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If an integrity violation in a message is detected by its recipient, the message MAY be rejected with a 403 (Forbidden) response if it is a request, or any existing dialog MAY be terminated.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: UAs SHOULD notify users of this circumstance and request explicit guidance on how to proceed.
actions: notify user of integrity violation circumstance
request explicit guidance on how to proceed

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The message must first be decrypted, and the "inner" From header field MUST be used as an index.
actions: use inner From header field as index for S/MIME key lookup

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In order to provide end-to-end integrity, encrypted "message/sip" MIME bodies SHOULD be signed by the sender.
actions: wrap in multipart/signed MIME body containing encrypted body and pkcs7-mime signature

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Bob registers on start-up. Bob's softphone sends REGISTER to the registrar.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The registrar responds with a 200 OK.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The registration expires after two hours (Expires: 7200).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The media session between Alice and Bob is now established.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: F1 INVITE Alice -> atlanta.com proxy; F2 100 Trying atlanta.com proxy -> Alice. Alice sends INVITE and receives 100 Trying provisional response.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: F6 180 Ringing Bob -> biloxi.com proxy; F8 180 Ringing atlanta.com proxy -> Alice. 180 Ringing propagated back to Alice.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: F9 200 OK Bob -> biloxi.com proxy ... F11 200 OK atlanta.com proxy -> Alice; F12 ACK Alice -> Bob. Alice receives 200 OK to INVITE and sends ACK; the media session is now established.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: F13 BYE Bob -> Alice; F14 200 OK Alice -> Bob. Bob sends BYE to terminate the established session; Alice responds with 200 OK.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once a dialog has been established by initial messaging, subsequent requests can be sent that modify the state of the dialog and/or session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once the BYE is received by its target, the session will be torn down prematurely.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Forged re-INVITEs that alter the session (possibly to reduce session security or redirect media streams as part of a wiretapping attack).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: failure to validate a certificate SHOULD result in the failure of the request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When used as the Request-URI of a request, the SIPS scheme signifies that each hop over which the request is forwarded, until the request reaches the SIP entity responsible for the domain portion of the Request-URI, must be secured with TLS; once it reaches the domain in question it is handled in accordance with local security and routing policy, quite possibly using TLS for any last hop to a UAS.
actions: Secure each forwarding hop with TLS until request reaches SIP entity responsible for Request-URI domain

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The use of SIPS in particular entails that mutual TLS authentication SHOULD be employed, as SHOULD the ciphersuite TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Certificates received in the authentication process SHOULD be validated with root certificates held by the client; failure to validate a certificate SHOULD result in the failure of the request.
actions: Validate received certificate against root certificates held by client

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Users that distribute a SIPS URI as an address-of-record may elect to operate devices that refuse requests over insecure transports.
actions: Refuse request received over insecure transport

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: All SIP elements that support TLS MUST have a mechanism for validating certificates received during TLS negotiation; this entails possession of one or more root certificates issued by certificate authorities (preferably well-known distributors of site certificates comparable to those that issue root certificates for web browsers).
actions: validate certificate received during TLS negotiation

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a UA attempts to contact a proxy server, redirect server, or registrar, the UAC SHOULD initiate a TLS connection over which it will send SIP messages.
actions: send SIP messages over TLS connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In some architectures, UASs MAY receive requests over such TLS connections as well.
actions: receive SIP request over TLS connection

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a UA comes online and registers with its local administrative domain, it SHOULD establish a TLS connection with its registrar.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The registrar SHOULD offer a certificate to the UA; when it receives the TLS Certificate message, the UA SHOULD verify the certificate and inspect the site identified by the certificate.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the certificate is invalid, revoked, or if it does not identify the appropriate party, the UA MUST NOT send the REGISTER message and otherwise proceed with the registration.
statements.invariant_cond: session.state = CERTIFICATE_VERIFICATION & (certificate.invalid = true | certificate.revoked = true | certificate.identifies_appropriate_party = false)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The UA then creates a REGISTER request that SHOULD be addressed to a Request-URI corresponding to the site certificate received from the registrar. When the UA sends the REGISTER request over the existing TLS connection...

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The registrar SHOULD challenge the request with a 401 (Proxy Authentication Required) response. When the UAC receives the challenge, it SHOULD either prompt the user for credentials or take an appropriate credential from a keyring.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once the registration has been accepted by the registrar, the UA SHOULD leave this TLS connection open.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When a valid certificate has been provided by the registrar, the UA creates a REGISTER request and sends it over the existing TLS connection.
actions: address Request-URI to site certificate domain

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The registrar SHOULD challenge the request with a 401 (Proxy Authentication Required) response.
actions: inspect realm parameter in Proxy-Authenticate header

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once the registration has been accepted by the registrar, the UA SHOULD leave this TLS connection open.
actions: leave TLS connection open for incoming requests

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a UA comes online and registers with its local administrative domain, it SHOULD establish a TLS connection with its registrar (Section 10 describes how the UA reaches its registrar).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The registrar SHOULD offer a certificate to the UA, and the site identified by the certificate MUST correspond with the domain in which the UA intends to register; for example, if the UA intends to register the address-of-record 'alice@atlanta.com', the site certificate must identify a host within the atlanta.com domain (such as sip.atlanta.com).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When it receives the TLS Certificate message, the UA SHOULD verify the certificate and inspect the site identified by the certificate.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the certificate is invalid, revoked, or if it does not identify the appropriate party, the UA MUST NOT send the REGISTER message and otherwise proceed with the registration.
statements.pre_cond: certificate.invalid = true | certificate.revoked = true | certificate.wrong_party = true

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UA then creates a REGISTER request that SHOULD be addressed to a Request-URI corresponding to the site certificate received from the registrar.
actions: set REGISTER Request-URI to domain identified by site certificate

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the UA sends the REGISTER request over the existing TLS connection, the registrar SHOULD challenge the request with a 401 (Proxy Authentication Required) response.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the UAC receives the challenge, it SHOULD either prompt the user for credentials or take an appropriate credential from a keyring corresponding to the "realm" parameter in the challenge.
actions: prompt user for credentials or retrieve credential from keyring matching challenge realm

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the Digest credentials have been inserted into an appropriate Proxy-Authorization header field, the REGISTER should be resubmitted to the registrar.
actions: resubmit REGISTER request with Proxy-Authorization header containing Digest credentials

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the registration has been accepted by the registrar, the UA SHOULD leave this TLS connection open provided that the registrar also acts as the proxy server to which requests are sent for users in this administrative domain.
actions: retain existing TLS connection open for subsequent inbound request delivery

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Each side of the connection SHOULD verify and inspect the certificate of the other. Once TLS negotiation has completed, resulting in a secure channel between the two proxies, the atlanta.com proxy can forward the INVITE request to biloxi.com.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Assuming that the client has completed the registration process described in the preceding section, it SHOULD reuse the TLS connection to the local proxy server when it sends an INVITE request to another user.
actions: reuse existing TLS connection to local proxy server for INVITE

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UA SHOULD reuse cached credentials in the INVITE to avoid prompting the user unnecessarily.
actions: include cached credentials in INVITE request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the local outbound proxy server has validated the credentials presented by the UA in the INVITE, it SHOULD inspect the Request-URI to determine how the message should be routed (see [4]).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The local outbound proxy server at atlanta.com SHOULD therefore establish a TLS connection with the remote proxy server at biloxi.com.
actions: establish TLS connection with remote proxy server at biloxi.com

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Since both of the participants in this TLS connection are servers that possess site certificates, mutual TLS authentication SHOULD occur.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each side of the connection SHOULD verify and inspect the certificate of the other, noting the domain name that appears in the certificate for comparison with the header fields of SIP messages.
actions: record domain name from certificate for comparison with SIP header fields

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The atlanta.com proxy server, for example, SHOULD verify at this stage that the certificate received from the remote side corresponds with the biloxi.com domain.
actions: verify that remote certificate domain corresponds with biloxi.com domain

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy server at biloxi.com SHOULD inspect the certificate of the proxy server at atlanta.com in turn and compare the domain asserted by the certificate with the "domainname" portion of the From header field in the INVITE request.
actions: compare certificate domain with From header field domainname portion of INVITE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The biloxi proxy MAY have a strict security policy that requires it to reject requests that do not match the administrative domain from which they have been proxied.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Once the INVITE has been approved by the biloxi proxy, the proxy server SHOULD identify the existing TLS channel, if any, associated with the user targeted by this request (in this case "bob@biloxi.com").
actions: identify existing TLS channel associated with target user

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Before they forward the request, both proxy servers SHOULD add a Record-Route header field to the request so that all future requests in this dialog will pass through the proxy servers.
actions: add Record-Route header field referencing proxy to request prior to forwarding

statements.subject: session
statements.description: a secure dialog begins after Bob replies authenticating himself to Carol

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Carol's UA SHOULD initiate a TLS connection with the biloxi proxy directly when she wishes to send an INVITE, and when her UA receives a certificate from the biloxi proxy, it SHOULD be verified normally before she passes her INVITE across the TLS connection
actions: initiate TLS connection with biloxi proxy

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The biloxi proxy has a policy for Bob that all non-authenticated requests should be redirected to the appropriate contact address registered against 'bob@biloxi.com'
statements.post_cond: redirection response sent with contact address <sip:bob@192.0.2.4>
actions: send redirection response with registered contact address

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Bob receives the INVITE, his UA inspects and recognizes the From header field and subsequently matches a locally cached certificate with the one presented in the signature of the body of the INVITE; he replies in similar fashion, authenticating himself to Carol, and a secure dialog begins
statements.trigger: INVITE received with matching signature certificate
actions: match locally cached certificate against body signature

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When Carol wishes to send an INVITE to "bob@biloxi.com", her UA SHOULD initiate a TLS connection with the biloxi proxy directly (using the mechanism described in [4] to determine how to best to reach the given Request-URI).
actions: Initiate TLS connection with biloxi proxy directly using Request-URI resolution mechanism

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When her UA receives a certificate from the biloxi proxy, it SHOULD be verified normally before she passes her INVITE across the TLS connection.
actions: Pass INVITE across TLS connection only after successful verification

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The biloxi proxy MAY also have a strict policy that precludes it from even bothering to challenge requests that do not have biloxi.com in the "domainname" portion of the From header field - it treats these users as unauthenticated.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Carol SHOULD then establish a TCP connection with the designated address and send a new INVITE with a Request-URI containing the received contact address (recomputing the signature in the body as the request is readied).
statements.post_cond: tcp_connection.established = true & new_INVITE.sent = true & signature.recomputed = true
actions: Establish TCP connection with designated contact address
Send new INVITE with Request-URI set to received contact address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: UAs and proxy servers SHOULD challenge questionable requests with only a single 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required), forgoing the normal response retransmission algorithm, and thus behaving statelessly towards unauthenticated requests.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: To address these concerns, it is RECOMMENDED that recipients of a request whose Request-URI contains a SIP or SIPS URI inspect the To header field value to see if it contains a SIPS URI (though note that it does not constitute a breach of security if this URI has the same scheme but is not equivalent to the URI in the To header field).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Recipients MAY also inspect the Via header chain in order to double-check whether or not TLS was used for the entire request path until the local administrative domain was reached.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the UAS has reason to believe that the scheme of the Request-URI has been improperly modified in transit, the UA SHOULD notify its user of a potential security breach.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: As a further measure to prevent downgrade attacks, entities that accept only SIPS requests MAY also refuse connections on insecure ports.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a UAC wishes to terminate a call before it has been answered, it sends CANCEL.
statements.trigger: UAC wishes to terminate call before answered

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the original INVITE still returns a 2xx, the UAC then sends BYE.
statements.trigger: 2xx received for INVITE after CANCEL sent

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a user sends an INVITE and then a CANCEL, the INVITE transaction still terminates normally.
statements.trigger: CANCEL sent for in-progress INVITE transaction
actions: INVITE transaction terminates normally (independently of CANCEL transaction)

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UAS needs to respond to the original INVITE request with a 487 response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: RFC 2543 allowed the UAS not to send a response to INVITE when a BYE was received. That is disallowed here. The original INVITE needs a response.
statements.trigger: BYE received during active INVITE transaction

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A UA cannot send a BYE for a call until it has received an ACK for the initial INVITE.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A UA or proxy cannot send CANCEL for a transaction until it gets a provisional response for the request.
statements.trigger: UA or proxy wishes to send CANCEL

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: Proxies no longer forward a 6xx immediately on receiving it. Instead, they CANCEL pending branches immediately. In all cases except this race condition, the result will be the same - the 6xx is forwarded upstream.
actions: forward 6xx upstream (after cancelling branches, not immediately on receipt)

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: A proxy MUST forward provisional responses from 101 to 199 upstream.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Specifically, receipt of a 503 should trigger an attempt to contact the next element in the result of a DNS SRV lookup.
actions: attempt to contact next element in DNS SRV lookup result

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Added a 'glare handling' mechanism to deal with the case where both parties send each other a re-INVITE simultaneously. It uses the new 491 (Request Pending) error code.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: There were a variety of mechanisms described for handling failures at any time during a call; those are now generally unified. BYE is sent to terminate.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Only 2xx responses to INVITEs are retransmitted over TCP.
statements.trigger: 2xx response to INVITE sent over TCP

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Allowed a registrar to reject registrations with expirations that are too short in duration. Defined the 423 response code and the Min-Expires for this purpose.
statements.trigger: REGISTER received with expiration too short
